description:
One article's position in one search, with the features that put it there.

Identified by the pair (`search_id`, `article_id`) rather than by an id of its own: a result
only exists as part of a search, and a search holds at most one result per article.

The scores are all optional because the V1 ranking pipeline is deterministic and lexical;
`semantic_score` and `rerank_score` are filled in by the embedding and rerank stages that
arrive with the V2 search index.

A feature can be unknown, and is then stored as None rather than left out or written as 0: no
discovery provider says whether a paper was peer-reviewed yet, and 0 would say it was not
(v1-e08-t03-feature-ranking).

search_id.description: The search this result belongs to.
search_id.title: Search Id

total_score.description: Combined score from the configured ranking weights.
total_score.title: Total Score

lexical_score.description: BM25 relevance of title and snippet.
lexical_score.title: Lexical Score

source_quality_features.description: Named ranking features and their values, for example recency, peer_reviewed, open_access, citations, provider_agreement; None where a feature is unknown, which is not the same as 0. Never a hidden credibility score.
source_quality_features.title: Source Quality Features

explanation.description: Human-readable reason for the rank, e.g. "recent (3 days), peer-reviewed".
explanation.title: Explanation

providers.description: Providers that returned this article; more than one means agreement.
providers.title: Providers

title: SearchResult
